severity: ROOT CAUSE of the visible hand shaking -- and a candidate cause of the noise floor
claim: RL fine-tuning induced a ~1.7 Hz open-close oscillation of the fingers that neither the demonstrations nor the SFT policy contain. The visible 'hand shaking' is not jitter, noise, or chunk-boundary jerk: it is the RL policy's predicted finger trajectory pumping ~0.6 rad every 30-step chunk.

measurement.protocol: same probe, same frozen condition 21, deterministic, full 690-step episode; finger joint 47 (1:1 with the policy's raw finger command via coupling=1.0)
measurement.spectral: 92% of the RLPD finger-command energy sits below 2 Hz with the pump at ~1.7 Hz (once per 0.6 s chunk); sign-flip rate 0.12, i.e. smooth large swings, not high-frequency noise
measurement.demonstration_behaviour: finger at 0.00 through the reach, closes 0 -> 1.30 rad over ~1 s, then holds rock-steady for the remainder of the episode
measurement.demo_bandwidth: 97.6% of demonstrated hand-signal energy below 1.0 Hz

attribution: SFT swing 0.065 vs RLPD 0.580 under identical execution: the oscillation is CREATED by RL fine-tuning, not inherited. Mechanism consistent with the literature (CAPS, Mysore et al., ICRA 2021, arXiv:2012.06644): exploration noise (std 0.2) on the hand dims enters the replay buffer, the reward contains no action-smoothness term, and the actor update fits the roughness.

why_earlier_fixes_failed.chunk_blending: fixed the boundary discontinuity (0.90 -> 0.15 rad) but the pump lives INSIDE the chunk; A/B correctly showed no effect
why_earlier_fixes_failed.why_it_looked_like_jitter: the retargeter drives proximal+intermediate from one command (coupling 1.0), doubling the visual amplitude on the fingers

connections: Candidate cause of the post-grasp nondeterminism noise floor: a hand pumping 0.58 rad/chunk around a 20 mm barrel makes contact outcomes chaotic (carry Jaccard 0.066 across identical runs) while the pre-contact stage stays reproducible (grasp Jaccard 0.99).
Candidate cause of grasp-never-becomes-transport: the object is squeezed and released repeatedly mid-hold.
The SFT stochastic successes are consistent: a smooth hand plus sampled arm variation.

fixes.execution_layer_now: rlinf/envs/isaaclab/tasks/g1_piston_action_filter.py -- demonstration-envelope filter: causal 2nd-order low-pass at f_c=1.2 Hz + slew cap 0.175/step, every constant measured from the 11 demos (cutoff chosen as the highest halving the measured pump while tracking demos to <0.05 RMSE and closing a grasp to 90% in 0.52 s). Carries state across chunks, so it subsumes blending. 11 unit tests, incl. halving the swing on the real recorded commands.
fixes.training_time_future: CAPS-style temporal smoothness penalty on consecutive actions in the SAC/RLPD actor loss; removes the pathology at the source but needs retraining (~11 h/arm).

validation_in_flight: In-sim A/B: RLPD@415k, frozen 25 conditions, deterministic, FILTER on -- judged against the well-characterised 8-run unfiltered baseline distribution (grasp 0.995 +/- 0.014, carry 0.195 +/- 0.122). Questions: does grasp survive the ~0.3 s filter lag; does damping the pump move carry above the baseline range.

dose_response.observation: SAC (no demonstration replay) oscillates 1.594 rad/chunk -- nearly the full finger range (limit 1.7) -- while RLPD (50% demonstration transitions per batch) oscillates 0.580, about 3x less, under identical execution and reward.
dose_response.interpretation: Demonstration replay partially protects action smoothness during RL fine-tuning. With no smoothness term in the reward and Gaussian exploration noise entering the replay, the demo fraction is the only thing anchoring the actor to demonstration-like action dynamics.
dose_response.caveat: n=1 checkpoint per algorithm at different training budgets (415k vs 690k); a training-time confound (budget) is not excluded. The earlier per-checkpoint probes suggest the oscillation grows with training in both algorithms.
